prose: A write-up from pwn.ai shows an escape from Firecracker, the microVM meant to isolate untrusted code, achieving root code execution on the host. Building on a host-memory primitive from Part 1, the authors find Firecracker in memory and take over a live vCPU thread: while the thread sits in the KVM_RUN ioctl, its saved registers (pt_regs) control where it resumes, so altering them makes it run a chosen call on return. Firecracker keeps running and the VM stays reachable over SSH. It is tied to a CVE identifier in the post.
highlights: Escape from a Firecracker microVM to root on the host
Hijacks a vCPU thread by editing saved registers during KVM_RUN
Firecracker and the VM keep running
